Fry the cumin and turmeric in the oil until aromatic, add the tomatoes, and cook down until the sauce darkens and thickens.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer until it glosses and loosens.
Halve the eggs into the sauce, warm them through until a food thermometer reads 160 °F, and serve with rice, bread, or a spoon.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Soak the beans overnight, then simmer them gently in fresh water until tender all the way through but not splitting.
Drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water, and fold the beans into a bean pot with the whole onion, molasses, brown sugar, the cubed salt pork and enough liquid to show at the surface.

Bake with the lid on, checking once to top up water, until the sauce has gone deep mahogany and thick enough to coat a spoon, and a food thermometer in a cube of salt pork reads at least 145 °F (63 °C).

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Rest the pot 3 minutes, then season at the end only — the pork has been salting the pot all along — and serve with brown bread or toast.

title: Barbecue Pulled Pork with Vinegar Slaw

steps.text: Rub the shoulder the night before, or at least an hour ahead, with the paprika, brown sugar and salt.
Roast it low in a covered pan with a splash of water, fat cap up, until the bone pulls free and a food thermometer in the thickest part reads well past 145 °F (63 °C) with the meat slack and giving.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: While it rests for at least 3 minutes, shred the cabbage and dress it with the yogurt, a slug of the vinegar, salt and pepper.
Pull the pork into shreds with two forks, moisten with the pan juices sharpened by more vinegar, and pile onto toasted buns with the slaw spilling over.

title: Red Wine Beef Daube with Carrots

steps.text: Marinate the chuck in the wine with the onion halves for an hour on the counter, turning once.
Lift the meat out, pat it dry, and brown it hard in the oil; strain the marinade and keep the wine.
Return everything to the pot with the carrot batons, cover, and braise at a tremble until the meat gives under a spoon and a food thermometer in the thickest piece reads well past 145 °F (63 °C).

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Rest the meat at least 3 minutes, taste the sauce for depth, and serve with the carrots and something plain — potatoes or wide noodles — beside.
Brown the pork cubes in a little oil, then soften the diced onion in the same pot.

Add the chipotle and tomatoes, cook down dark, then return the pork with water to cover and simmer until the cubes loosen at the edges and a food thermometer in a thick cube reads well past 145 °F (63 °C).

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Add the hominy and warm through so it drinks the broth, then let the pot rest 3 minutes off the heat.
Serve in wide bowls with cabbage, lime, oregano and a spoon of the chili simmer water over each.

title: Crispy Fish Tacos with Lime Slaw

steps.text: Pat the fillets dry, press them in the cornmeal seasoned with salt and chili powder, and rest them five minutes.
Shred the cabbage and toss with the lime juice, yogurt and salt — it should sit and soften while you cook.
Pan-fry the fillets in oil until the crust sets and a food thermometer in the thick end reads 145 °F, flipping once.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Break the fish into the warm tortillas and bury it in slaw; hot sauce non-negotiable.
Poach the breast in salted water until a food thermometer reads 165 °F, then shred it and keep the poaching water.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Fry the tomatoes with the chipotle and a ladle of poaching water until the sauce turns brick and loosens.
Dip each tortilla in the sauce, fill with chicken and onion, roll, and lay them seam-down in a baking dish.
Pour the rest of the sauce over, shower with cheddar, and bake until bubbling at the edges.
Rest five minutes, then serve with crema and shredded lettuce.
Tear the tortillas and fry them in the oil until they stiffen and spot; lift onto a towel.
Fry the tomatoes with the chipotle until the sauce darkens, then fold the crisped tortillas through it loosely — some crunch must survive.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan until the whites set and a food thermometer reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Plate the sauced chips with an egg on each, crumbled feta, and sliced onion in lime.
Char the corn hard in a dry skillet, letting it blacken in patches before each toss.
Off the heat, fold in the yogurt, crumbled feta, chili and a hard squeeze of lime.
Let the salad sit ten minutes so the corn drinks the dressing, then eat with tortilla chips or a spoon.

title: Sopa de Lima-Style Chicken and Lime Soup

steps.text: Poach the breast in the stock with half a sliced onion and the oregano until a food thermometer reads 165 °F; lift out to rest.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Toast the tortilla strips in the oven until they snap.
Shred the chicken back into the broth and bring it to a steam, then kill the heat and squeeze the limes in — off the heat keeps the soup bright.
Serve with the tortilla strips scattered over and more lime at the table.
Blend the tomatoes with the chipotle, cumin, garlic and a cup of water into a rough sauce.

Sear the chuck on every side in a Dutch oven, pour the sauce over with water to cover, and braise covered in a low oven until the beef falls when nudged and a food thermometer in the thickest part reads well past 145 °F (63 °C).

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Rest the beef at least 3 minutes, skim the fat from the broth, shred the beef, and keep both warm.
Dip the tortillas in the reserved fat, crisping them in a hot pan, fill with beef and onion, and serve with the broth in cups alongside.
Fry the tomatoes with the chili until the sauce darkens and loses its raw edge.
Warm the beans in the sauce, then hold on the back burner.
Crisp the tortillas in a little oil until they fold without cracking.
Fry the eggs until the whites set and a food thermometer reads 160 °F, and build: tortilla, beans, egg, sauce.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Poach the shrimp in well-salted simmering water just until a food thermometer at the centre reads 145 °F, then chill them in cold water and drain.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Blend the chili with the cilantro, half the cucumber and the lime juice with a splash of water into a bright green sauce.
Toss the chilled shrimp with the sauce and the remaining cucumber sliced paper thin, and let the bowl sit in the fridge for ten minutes.
Serve cold in shallow bowls with tortilla chips to scoop — cold, sharp, and just set.
Boil the potato cubes until a fork gives, then crisp them in the butter until the edges fry brown.
Scramble the eggs gently in the same pan until a food thermometer reads 160 °F (71 °C).

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Warm the tortillas, load with potatoes, eggs and cheese, and roll them tight in foil.
Eat one now; freeze the other and reheat from frozen until a food thermometer in the middle reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Cubed eggplant, salted and sweated for ten minutes, then fried in the oil until it turns deep gold and creamy within.
Cook the tomatoes down in the same pan with a pinch of sugar until they sweeten and darken.
Boil the penne a minute shy, then finish it in the sauce with a ladle of pasta water and half the basil.
Serve with torn ricotta salata or a spoonful of ricotta, the rest of the basil, and pepper.

title: Tuscan White Beans on Garlic Toasts

steps.text: Warm the beans with the crushed garlic, a ribbon of oil and a splash of water, mashing a few for creaminess.
Toast the bread hard and rub each slice with the raw garlic clove while hot.
Pile the beans on the toasts with the diced raw tomato, salt, and a final pour of oil.
Eat standing up — this is a lunch that believes it is a snack.
Split the breast into two cutlets, pound them even, and press them through beaten egg into the breadcrumbs mixed with the parmesan.
Shallow-fry in oil until the crust takes on real color and a food thermometer at the centre of the thickest cutlet reads 165 °F; drain briefly.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Spoon the cooked tomatoes around the cutlets in a skillet, lay the mozzarella on each, and cover off the heat until it melts.
Serve with pasta or bread, and cut into the crust while the cheese still pulls.
Soften the carrot coins and diced onion in the oil, add the tomatoes, and cook down for ten minutes.
Pour in the stock and beans and simmer until the carrot is tender.
Add the zucchini and pasta together and cook until the pasta is just done — the soup thickens as it stands.
Season hard, finish with parmesan and oil, and eat with the last of the bread.
Brown the beef hard in oil, breaking it small, until it takes on real color.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Add the gochujang and fry it in the fat until it darkens a shade, then pour in half a cup of water with the soy.
Cubed tofu, pressed dry, slides in gently — simmer, shaking the pan rather than stirring, until the sauce clings.
Finish with the green onions and a thread of sesame oil, and eat over rice.
Split and pound the breast into two even cutlets; press them through beaten egg into the panko and press hard so the crust holds.
Shallow-fry in oil, turning once, until the crust is deep gold and a food thermometer at the centre reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Shred the cabbage fine and dress it with the soy and rice vinegar — it should taste sharp and cold.
Rest the cutlets five minutes on a rack so the crust stays crisp, slice across, and serve with the cabbage and rice.
Crisp the ground pork in a hot pan with a spoon of oil, breaking it small, until it sticks and browns in patches.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Boil the noodles and drain, keeping a mug of the water.
Whisk the peanut butter with the soy, chili, sugar and hot water into a pourable sauce.
Toss the noodles through the sauce, loosen with the noodle water, and crown with the pork and green onions.
Mix the yogurt with the garam masala, ginger, lemon juice and salt, and coat the thighs in it for at least twenty minutes.
Roast the thighs on a rack, basting once with the last of the marinade, until a food thermometer at the bone reads 165 °F and the crust blisters.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Rest five minutes, then serve with lemon wedges, sliced onion and mint chutney if you have it.
Soften the diced onion in the oil until it edges toward brown, then fry the spices in the pan for a breath.
Add the tomatoes and cook until the oil separates and the sauce turns brick.
Fold in the chickpeas with a splash of water and simmer until the sauce hugs them — squash a few to thicken.
Serve with rice or flatbread, lemon, and sliced onion in lime.
Soften the diced onion and chili in the butter until they turn translucent and sweet.
Add the cumin and diced tomato and cook down to a rough masala.
Beat the eggs with salt, pour in, and stir slowly — soft curds, never dry — pulling the pan off as soon as a food thermometer reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Serve on buttered toast or rolled in flatbread, with black pepper and more chili.
Rinse the rice and lentils together until the water clears.
Warm the ghee with the cumin, add the cubed potato and turmeric, then the grains with three cups of salted water.
Simmer gently, stirring once or twice, until the pot turns soft and porridge-like and the potato gives.
Finish with pepper and a spoon of ghee, and eat with pickle and yogurt.
Simmer the lentils in salted water until tender but whole, then drain.
Fry the sliced onions in the oil, patiently, until they go far past gold into crisp mahogany — half the pot is the point.
Add the rice and cumin to the pan, stir in the lentils with two cups of water, and cook covered until the rice is done.
Rest covered for ten minutes, then fork through the remaining crispy onions and eat with yogurt and cucumber.
Marinate the thighs in yogurt, lemon, garlic, cumin and salt for at least twenty minutes, longer if the day allows.
Sear them hard in a hot skillet, then lower the heat and cook through until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Rest the thighs, then slice across into ribbons that catch the pan juices.
Build bowls on rice or flatbread with pickled onion, cucumber and the garlic-yogurt sauce thinned with lemon.
Cut everything into generous chunks, toss hard with the oil, oregano and salt, and pile into a roasting tin — crowded is correct.
Roast, turning once, until the edges blacken and the potatoes give under a knife.
Crumble the feta over the hot vegetables so it slumps, and return for two minutes.
Serve warm, not hot, with bread to chase the oil and lemon over everything.
Soften the diced carrot and onion in the oil with the cumin until the spice smells toasted.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer until the lentils collapse and the soup turns silky.
Kill the heat and add the lemon juice — off the heat it stays bright instead of bitter.
Blend half the pot if you like it smooth, season hard, and eat with warm bread.
Season the thighs and sear them skin-side down in a cold-start skillet so the fat renders and the skin crisps.
Flip, add the garlic, and cook until a food thermometer reads 165 °F; move them to a warm plate.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Pour off the excess fat, then bubble the honey and soy in the pan until it glazes a spoon.
Return the thighs to be turned through the glaze, and serve over rice with the pan sauce and green onions.
Prick the potatoes, rub them with oil and salt, and bake directly on the rack until they give all the way through.
Steam the broccoli florets until just tender, then chop small.
Split the potatoes, fluff the insides with the butter, and fold in the yogurt, broccoli and most of the cheese.
Return to the oven until the cheese bubbles, and eat with the rest of the cheese and pepper over.
Mix the tuna with the lemon juice, a spoon of mayonnaise and pepper.
Pile onto the bread, cheese over, and toast under the broiler until the cheese blisters and the bread edges darken.
Cut corner to corner and eat while the toast still crackles.
Toast the bread until it holds a spread without bending.
Spread the peanut butter thickly to the corners while the toast is hot.
Lay the sliced banana over in overlapping rows and drizzle the honey in thin threads.
Cut into strips, pour the coffee strong, and eat with your feet up if the morning allows.
Boil the noodles, drain, and rinse them cold — cold water keeps them bouncy for a chilled bowl.
Whisk the peanut butter with the soy, vinegar, a pinch of sugar and hot water until pourable.
Toss the noodles through the sauce with the matchsticked cucumber and most of the green onions.
Chill for ten minutes if you can wait, then eat with the last of the onions over.

title: Egg Drop Soup with Green Onions

steps.text: Bring the stock to a bare simmer and slurry the cornstarch with cold water before adding it — lumps loiter otherwise.
Beat the eggs and pour them in a thin stream over a fork dragged through the surface, making ribbons.
Cook one more minute until the ribbons set and a food thermometer reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Season with white or black pepper and the green onions, and drink it from a large mug if the day is that kind.

title: Sausage and Peppers over Creamy Polenta

steps.text: Brown the sausages whole in a little oil, then lift out and slice into coins.
Cook the peppers and onion in the rendered fat until they slump and sweeten, then return the sausage coins and cook until a food thermometer in a thick coin reads 160 °F (71 °C).

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Meanwhile whisk the cornmeal into two cups of salted water and cook slowly, stirring the corners, until it thickens.
Beat the parmesan into the polenta, spoon it into bowls, and drag the sausage and peppers over with their oil.
Sear the chops in a hot skillet until they take on real color on both sides.
Lower the heat, melt the butter around them, and bury the chops in the sliced onion.
Pour the stock down the side of the pan, cover, and simmer gently until a food thermometer in the thickest part, away from the bone, reads 145 °F (63 °C); rest the chops 3 minutes.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Reduce the pan sauce to a spoon-coating glaze, taste it for salt, and pour it back over the chops.
Soften the diced pepper in the butter, then wilt the spinach through and tip it onto a plate.
Beat the eggs, pour them into the same pan, and stir slowly over low heat.
Pull the pan off as soon as a food thermometer reads 160 °F — the carryover finishes the curds.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Fold the vegetables and cheese through, season hard, and serve with toast.
Bring the stock with the diced carrot and celery to a simmer and slide the whole breast in.
Poach gently until a food thermometer at the centre reads 165 °F; lift the breast out to rest.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Add the rice to the broth and cook until the grains are tender and the soup has body.
Shred the chicken back in, season generously, and finish with black pepper and dill if you have it.
Soften the diced onion first — raw onion in a meatloaf stays raw.
Mix the beef with the onion, breadcrumbs, egg, salt and pepper using a light hand; overwork it and it tightens up.
Shape into a small loaf on a lined tin and bake until a food thermometer at the centre reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Bubble the tomatoes down to a quick glaze and paint it over the loaf for the last ten minutes.
Rest ten minutes before slicing — it slices cleaner warm, not hot.
Poach the breast in salted water until a food thermometer reads 165 °F, then shred it.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Fry the sliced onion until it edges toward brown, add the chipotle and tomatoes, and cook the sauce down dark.
Fold the shredded chicken through the sauce and let it drink for a few minutes.
Crisp the tortillas in a little oil until they snap, and load them with the tinga, crema, and shredded lettuce.
Rinse and drain the beans, then warm them with the corn and a pinch of cumin and chili.
Scatter the mixture and the cheese over two tortillas, cap with the others, and press.
Cook the quesadillas in a dry skillet, weighted with a second pan, until the cheese melts and the bottoms blister.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and lime — the wedge shape is half the pleasure.
Start the rice, seasoned assertively, and hold it covered.
Slice the breast into strips, toss with oil, cumin, chili powder and salt, and rest it while the pan heats.
Sear the chicken strips hard in a screaming-hot skillet until a food thermometer reads 165 °F; lift them out.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Cook the peppers and onion in the same pan until they char at the edges, then squeeze the lime over everything.
Build the bowls on the rice and finish with avocado if you have one.

title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio with Spinach

steps.text: Boil the spaghetti in aggressively salted water.
Warm the sliced garlic in the oil over low heat until it turns pale gold — never brown, it bitter — with the chili.
Wilt the spinach into the garlic oil in handfuls.
Drag the pasta straight from the pot into the pan with a ladle of its water and toss hard until the sauce clings — the starch does the work.
Sear the thighs skin-side down until the skin is deep gold; lift out.
Cook the mushrooms dry in the rendered fat until they squeak, then add the onion and pepper.
Pour in the tomatoes, return the thighs skin-up, and simmer covered until a food thermometer at the bone reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Uncover for the last minutes so the sauce thickens, and serve over polenta or pasta.
Drain and rinse the beans, then dress them while still cool from the rinse so the dressing soaks in.
Cut the tomatoes into rough chunks and salt them in a colander for a few minutes; the drip goes in the dressing, not on the plate.
Fold everything together with the torn mozzarella, the basil, a hard glug of oil and pepper.
Let the salad sit ten minutes before eating — beans need time more than they need anything else.
Start the rice; stir-fry waits for no one.
Slice the breast thin across the grain and toss with a spoon of cornstarch and a splash of water — the slurry keeps it tender.
Stir-fry the chicken in a very hot pan until a food thermometer reads 165 °F, then lift out.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Blister the broccoli in the same pan with the ginger and garlic, splash in the soy with a little water, and return the chicken to gloss it all.
Cook the rice and spread it on a plate to steam off — wet rice steams itself into mush in the pan.
Sear the shrimp in a hot oiled pan just until a food thermometer reads 145 °F; lift out.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Scramble the eggs in the same pan until a food thermometer reads 160 °F (71 °C), then add the rice and break it up, letting it toast against the metal.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Fold in the peas, shrimp, soy and green onions, and eat straight from the pan if no one is watching.
Press the tofu under a weight while you start the rice; drier tofu takes color.
Cook the mushrooms dry until they brown in patches, then add oil, ginger and garlic.
Cubed tofu goes in with the soy and half a cup of water; simmer, shaking the pan, until the sauce reduces to a glaze.
Finish with the green onions and a thread of sesame oil, and serve on the rice.
Toss the cubed chicken with the ginger, half the garam masala and salt, and let it sit while the pan heats.
Sear the cubes hard, in batches if they crowd, until a food thermometer reads 165 °F; lift out.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Cook the tomatoes with the remaining garam masala until the sauce darkens and the raw edge cooks off.
Lower the heat, stir in the cream, return the chicken, and warm through gently — a hard boil splits the sauce.
Serve over rice with something fresh — cucumber in lime — against the richness.

title: Red Lentil Dal with Spinach and Coconut

steps.text: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear, then simmer them with the turmeric and salt in three cups of water.
When the lentils collapse, whisk in the coconut milk and let the dal come back to a murmur.
Wilt the spinach through in handfuls, then season with black pepper and a squeeze of lime.
Serve over rice with pickle on the side — the dal improves as it stands, so make it first and eat it last.
Warm the chickpeas with the cumin, chili and salt until they dry out and take the spice.
Toss the warm chickpeas with the diced tomato, cucumber, lime juice and most of the cilantro.
Let the chaat sit five minutes so the lime pulls everything together, then eat cold or warm with crushed tortilla chips for crunch.
Heat the oven hard and toss the quartered potatoes with the oil, oregano and salt in the roasting tin.
Nestle the thighs in, skin up, and roast until a food thermometer at the bone reads 165 °F and the potatoes give under a knife.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Squeeze the lemon over everything and rest the tin for five minutes so the potatoes drink the juices.
Eat from the tin with bread, standing over the counter — the best pan juices never survive a serving dish.
Chop the cucumber, tomatoes and pepper into a rough, even dice and salt them in the bowl — the salt draws a light juice that becomes the dressing.
Add the oregano, oil and a hard squeeze of lemon if you have it, and toss with your hands.
Crumble the feta over last so it stays in identifiable pieces, and eat with bread to wipe the bowl.
Warm the garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes with salt and a pinch of sugar, and cook the sauce down until it loses its raw edge.
Season the fillets, lay them into the sauce in a small baking dish, and spoon sauce over to cover.
Bake until the flesh flakes at the touch of a fork and a food thermometer at the centre reads 145 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Finish with the lemon juice and eat with bread or rice — the sauce is the point.
Brown the thighs in an oven-safe pan, then lift them out and soften the diced onion in the fat.
Stir the rice through the onion, pour in the stock, and lay the thighs back on top, skin up.
Bake covered until the rice has drunk the stock and a food thermometer at the bone reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Scatter the peas over for the last five minutes so they warm but keep their snap, and rest the pan before serving.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and wrap them in a towel to steam soft.
Beat the eggs with salt, then scramble them slowly in the butter, dragging the curds from the edges.
Pull the pan off as soon as a food thermometer reads 160 °F — soft curds, not dry ones.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (food-safety rulebook data/food-safety/rules.json, citation fsis-safe-temperature-chart)

steps.text: Fill the tortillas with the eggs and cheese, and finish with the cilantro and hot sauce.
Soak the noodles in hot water off the boil until they bend without snapping, then rinse them cold.
Whisk the soy with the lime juice, a pinch of sugar and a spoon of water into a light dressing.
Toss the noodles with the julienned carrot and cucumber and most of the dressing.
Pile into bowls with the cilantro over, and pour the last of the dressing at the table.
Cube the eggplant, salt it, and roast the pieces until they collapse and take color at the edges.

Dust the onions with the flour, cook it out, then add a cup and a half of water and bubble to a gravy; return the patties to warm through and serve over the potatoes.
Brown the beef hard, breaking it small, until the pan picks up a crust.

Pour in the tomatoes with half a cup of water, cover, and simmer until the potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Season sharp with salt and a splash of vinegar or lime, and serve with rice or in warm tortillas.
Cook the diced chicken with the onion and chili powder until a food thermometer reads 165 °F, then stir in the tomatoes and simmer to a thick filling.

Spread the filling in the pan, top with the cornmeal in a rough layer, and shower with the cheddar.
Bake until the cornmeal sets and the cheese browns, then rest ten minutes so it slices instead of slurries.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water and save a mug of the starchy water before draining.
Melt the butter with the sliced garlic over low heat until the garlic is gold but not brown — garlic turns bitter past gold.
Add the shrimp in one layer and cook just until a food thermometer reads 145 °F; they go from perfect to rubber in a minute.

steps.text: Toss the pasta into the pan with the lemon juice and splashes of pasta water until the sauce clings, and eat immediately.
Whisk the yogurt with the besan, turmeric and salt until smooth, then thin with three cups of water.
Bring the mixture to a simmer slowly, stirring so it never splits, and let it bubble gently to a light sauce.
Fry the cumin and chili flakes in ghee until fragrant and pour it over the soup — it should sizzle on contact.
Eat over rice with a spoonful of the crisp cumin on each bowl, and a squeeze of lime.
Season the cubed thighs and sear them in oil until browned all over; they finish in the sauce.

title: Eggs in Yogurt with Chili Butter

steps.text: Spread the yogurt on plates and let it come to cool room temperature while the eggs cook.
Fry the eggs in the butter until the whites set and a food thermometer at the yolk's edge reads 160 °F.

steps.text: Slide the eggs onto the yogurt and pour the chili-flecked butter from the pan over everything.
Finish with salt, dill or mint, and eat with bread before the yogurt warms through.

title: Warm Lentil Salad with Roasted Carrots

steps.text: Roast the thick carrot coins in oil, cumin and salt until they shrink and caramelize at the edges.
Simmer the lentils in salted water until tender but intact — a few minutes past al dente, never to mush.
Drain and dress the warm lentils with lemon juice, oil and a little grated garlic; warm lentils drink dressing properly.
Fold in the carrots and the green tops of the onions, crumble feta over if you keep it, and eat warm or tomorrow, cold.
Whisk the dry ingredients with a pinch of salt and a spoon of sugar; whisk the wet ones separately.
Combine with a few rough strokes — lumps are structure, overmixing is glue.
Cook in the buttered pan over medium heat until bubbles pop and the edges dry, then flip once more only.
Check the first pancake reaches a food thermometer's 160 °F, then stack, top with the honey-butter, and pour the rest of the honey over.

Stir-fry the mushrooms dry first so they squeak, then add the oil and the cabbage ribbons.
Season with the soy, a little vinegar and sugar, and cook until the cabbage wilts but still snaps.
Return the eggs, toss once, and let everyone build their own wrap — a food thermometer should read 160 °F before the filling lands in the first tortilla.

Blanch the broccoli florets briefly in the simmering rice-water's first boil or in a splash of water in the wok.
Stir-fry the chicken hard until a food thermometer reads 165 °F, add the ginger and garlic, then the broccoli.

Add the diced tomato and cook it down into the onion.
Stir in the beans with half a cup of their liquid or water, and simmer until the broth turns silky and the beans soften into it.
Season with lime and salt, shower with cilantro, and eat as a side that thinks it is a main.

title: Braised White Beans with Zucchini and Tomatoes

steps.text: Brown the zucchini chunks hard in oil so they color instead of weep, and lift them out.
Cook the garlic in the same oil, add the tomatoes with the oregano and salt, and simmer to a rough sauce.
Return the zucchini with the beans and a splash of water, and braise slowly until everything softens into one pot of stew.
Finish with raw olive oil and basil, and eat with bread — tonight it is a stew, tomorrow, cold from the fridge, it is a salad.
